ownerAction: The owner created the ChatGPT connector by selecting Authentication = No Auth, bypassing the OAuth configuration entirely. This was the owner's own act, not an implementer action.

whatIsNowProven.evidence: tunnel-client dispatcher forwarded commands to the MCP server at 14:11:23-14:11:25 with rpc_request_id values openai-mcp-discover, 1 and 0, plus an acknowledged notification.
whatIsNowProven.bridgeAcceptedThem: No new entries in bridge-refusals.jsonl since 2026-08-22T00:29 — the calls were accepted, not refused.
whatIsNowProven.meaning: ChatGPT reaches the private ProjectOS bridge through the OpenAI tunnel, and the bridge answers. The transport, the tunnel, the replacement tunnel association and the runtime key all work.

whatIsNOTProven.oauthBoundary: NOT EXERCISED AT ALL. No authorization page, no PIN, no code, no token exchange, no audience check.
whatIsNOTProven.ownerConsentGate: NOT IN THE PATH. The approval PIN is the mechanism by which the owner consents to a connector; under No Auth nothing ever asks for it.
whatIsNOTProven.criterion15AsSpecified: NOT PROVEN. C15 is about an owner-approved OAuth boundary, and this connection demonstrates the transport beneath it rather than the boundary itself.

whatActuallyAuthenticatedTheCalls.mechanism: The static installation bridge token, injected by tunnel-client via --mcp.extra-headers 'Authorization: env:PROJECTOS_BRIDGE_AUTH'.
whatActuallyAuthenticatedTheCalls.consequence: Under No Auth, ChatGPT itself presents no credential. Anything able to send commands down this tunnel reaches the bridge holding full bridge authority, with no per-connector consent step.
whatActuallyAuthenticatedTheCalls.previouslyFlagged: This is exactly the observability gap reported earlier: the bridge accepts either credential class and no safe diagnostic distinguishes them. Here that ambiguity is the whole point — a working connector under No Auth could easily be mistaken for a successful OAuth proof.

boundingFactorsStillIntact: The bridge exposes exactly seven read operations plus stop-work; the refusal log shows 'deploy' rejected with the full permitted list.
It is bound to project projectos and refuses any other project id.
It refuses free-text arguments, so nothing written in a conversation can become an instruction.
It refuses owner impersonation via a decidedBy argument.
8787 remains loopback-only; public /mcp remains 404; the tunnel is owner-owned and requires the runtime key.
residualRisk: Real but bounded. The exposure is read-only governed state plus stop-work, reachable by whoever controls the ChatGPT connector on the Plus workspace, without an owner approval step. It is not a path to mutation, credentials, the filesystem or arbitrary commands.
recommendation: Treat this as proof of the MCP channel, not of C15. If the OAuth boundary is wanted, Option S remains the route; if the gatekeeper accepts a token-authenticated channel instead, that is a change to what C15 means and is the gatekeeper's ruling to make, not the implementer's.
implementerActions: NONE — no source change, no tunnel change, no Cloudflare or DNS change, no commit, no push. The connector was created by the owner.
